331.t: Teagarden, the Army and the radio repair trade, then Ralph Flanagan
331.s: Discovering Jack Teagarden, uncertain direction, a father-advised radio repair trade, National Guard band, and the call from John Strophe leading to joining Ralph Flanagan.
331.q: Okay. Well I’ll just briefly say that trombone became my favorite instrument. I played the violin all the way through high school and even a little with the local symphony afterwards. But trombone became my favorite and I eventually dropped the violin all together. And my father brought home a…

331.t: Discovering Dixieland in New Orleans with George Girard and Al Hirt
331.s: Sitting in on Bourbon Street, an offer from George Girard's New Orleans Five, and later the front line of Al Hirt's band with Pete Fountain.
331.q: Yeah. Here I’ve only been with Flanagan one month and now I’m on Bourbon Street and I get another offer, and it took me about ten seconds to decide I’d rather play Dixieland than the big band. I finished the tour with Flanagan and four months later I came back to New Orleans and played with…

402.t: Willie Rosenblum's band and the wood block
402.s: Sal tells of replacing Godfrey in a Jewish band and Willie Rosenblum's rhythm.
402.q: Yeah, he played trumpet, or a Jew band. So, Goppsen, they quit the band to go with Leslie George, see. So they got me to play. It was a rock band, you know, I got to cut the mustard there. I went and played the band, the Jew band, see, with Willie. Willie was playing the Tulane band, the old…

577.t: The Beverly Gardens job in New Orleans
577.s: His only job in New Orleans before leaving again, a few months at Beverly Gardens with Dela Roe, Bonnie Potter and George Schilling.
577.q: About three months or something like that. And whose band was that one? I don't know who was the leader of the band here. It was like I tell you, Dela Roe on piano and Bonnie Potter on bass, George Shilling, and Paul Piquet, and I can't think of the dumbest name from them. I don't know who actually…

251.t: Why Hall joined Albert's band; gigs with Sidney Desvigne
251.s: Hall left for adventure as a single man and played only a few gigs with Desvigne; he spent little time in New Orleans.
251.ch: Baton Rouge and the Albert band
251.q: you know uh i don't know for some reason i just felt like i wanted to go you know the guys give me a bit off and told me what was happening and then i was like in celestan in new orleans i mean uh city does leave me in new orleans and uh wasn't very much happening so i said i was single you know in…

43.t: First cabaret job at Bucktown with Manuel Mineta's band
43.s: Her first nightclub job was in Bucktown, singing Dardanella with Manuel Mineta's band. They try to recall the other players, including Amos White on cornet and Zip on clarinet.
43.ch: Bucktown, Chicago and the cabaret years
43.q: Well, it's like I'm telling you, in the concerts, you see, when I was small, it was not, they never said about featured, they just had the show and all of us kids went on. But the first cabaret job, the first time I ever worked in a nightclub was right here in New Orleans out in Bucktown for…

778.t: First New Orleans job at the Pelican with Pop Silverstein
778.s: First job in New Orleans was at the Pelican with Papa Celestin, via her husband the drummer.
778.q: They may be doing it now, but they didn't. They sound like he was on the new, were you saying that? Yeah. Well anyway, that's enough of that old music stuff, until we get between the reels. Then we'll play a little four handed. Can you play bass while I play treble? Mm-hmm. Okay. Play bass while…

591.t: Houston, New Orleans and leaving for Europe in 1924
591.s: Playing around Houston and New Orleans with Jack Carey, One Eye Ollie and others before sailing for Europe in 1924.
591.q: So I played the, I can't call his name. He was looking for me not too long ago, a saxophone player. Had a band from Houston and we went on excursion there.

456.t: Hearing and learning New Orleans jazz, pick-up bands, Fazola
456.s: Lured to New Orleans by its jazz reputation, he learns the two-beat, plays Dixieland on weekend pick-up jobs, meets Fazola and plays Broadway shows at the Civic.
456.ch: New Orleans arrival, jazz and Fazola
456.q: Yeah. Just about that time. About forty-eight. I'd have to look it up in the files because, boy, I'm very bad with dates. Mm-hmm. I don't mean dates with girls, but I mean, as far as nineteen this, nineteen that, and June, and January. Yeah. Did you hear any jazz when you came down here? Oh, yeah.…

797.t: New Orleans revival style and trips to Preservation Hall
797.s: The Allen group plays New Orleans revival style, the music Ecklund heard on trips to New Orleans and Preservation Hall in the late 1960s.
797.q: That was New Orleans revival style, that’s what he likes. He plays kind of like George Lewis. That’s the music I heard in the late ‘60s when I was in college. I made a lot of trips to New Orleans on vacations and heard some of that music when it was still pretty decent, at Preservation Hall and all…

94.t: Sitting in with Papa Celestin and getting the job
94.s: When Celestin's band played Monroe, Moore sat in, and the missing trombonist's job became his.
94.q: When Celestin played the ballroom, they asked me to bring my horn and come and sit in, so I did. I sat in and low and behold I wanted to get off, I played enough horn for sitting in. So I turned around they had no trombone player, the trombone player had left. He had left and Celestin said, well,…
